goal: rev3: the VM is one execution domain behind the flow boundary: an Ops core inside the VM owns session management, the commit gate and the push gate; worker sessions inside the VM change files, test and commit but cannot push.
why: user 10-07 00:5x KST: make the VM the trust boundary; baseline says what, the VM creates the sessions it needs, works, commits, checks, pushes and reports; commit approval (VM-internal state) and push approval (publishing outside) are separate, push is the higher authority; existing gate/judge become the VM's internal policy enforcement point. Supersedes rev2 acceptance, keeps rev2 boundary rules.
acceptance: everything in rev2 still holds (boundary forms only, id/ref, no cloud read of VM internals, deterministic replay, restart without lost or duplicated messages, boundary change = new form version)
a worker session inside the VM can commit but any push attempt by it fails; only the VM Ops core can push, and only after the commit gate and the push gate both pass
the commit gate decides from tests, allowed paths, target branch, diff and the user policy, with zero model calls; its decision and evidence are recorded per commit

the push gate is a separate, higher check than the commit gate (target repo/ref allowed by the user policy, verdict passed, revert proven); each push is reported to the cloud as status/1 naming sha and ref

the VM Ops core creates and ends sessions itself within VM policy caps: max concurrent sessions, max child sessions, total session budget, session timeout, total token/USD budget, no duplicate session for the same work item; a request over any cap is refused and recorded as shadow/1 (rejected_by budget or policy)
every VM model call goes through the single gateway of DEV-VMAUTO (served model, tokens, USD per call)
constraints: rev3 stays ON HOLD exactly like rev2: no build starts until the user confirms from measurements that the token problem is solved (DEV/OPS-VMAUTO) and R0-baseline exists (R0FREEZE)

never two primaries: until a later cutover spec the cloud Dev/Ops hubs stay the authority and the VM takes no externally visible action (shadow); VM pushes go only to VM-owned shadow refs until cutover
the VM policy (budgets, caps, push-allowed repos/refs) is changed only by the user; no agent, session or VM component can alter it, and a change by anything else is rejected and recorded

no per-action user prompt inside the VM, but the user is never removed: over-budget or over-cap is refused (fail-closed) and reported; a kill switch and a direct user alarm path live outside what the VM measures and controls
work refused by the cloud platform is not re-routed through the VM; current cloud blockers (integrator push approval, Dev session git permission) are resolved by the user in those sessions
a model credential for the VM is a user question (status/1 blocker), never copied out of a session
LLM output inside the VM is a proposal only; commit, push and session decisions are deterministic
no VM model runs continuously until the user sets a budget (ASK-VM-COST)
